name: Hypomaturation Amelogenesis Imperfecta

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Amelogenesis Imperfecta

criteria.description: Presence of enamel with normal thickness but mottled, opaque, and discolored appearance
Enamel with reduced hardness leading to increased susceptibility to fracture and attrition
Radiographs showing enamel with radiodensity similar to dentin, indicating hypomaturation
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes such as MMP20 or KLK4

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of enamel with normal thickness but hypomatured appearance and radiographic evidence of enamel radiodensity similar to dentin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic testing can confirm subtype.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically yellow-brown or white opaque enamel

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal enamel thickness with reduced hardness
searchTerms: enamel that is thin but not hard
enamel with normal size but reduced strength

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiographic enamel radiodensity similar to dentin
searchTerms: enamel looks like dentin on x-ray
enamel density similar to inner tooth

common.notes: Leads to tooth sensitivity and functional impairment
Due to enamel defects exposing dentin
searchTerms: sensitive teeth to hot and cold

common.symptomName: Discoloration varying from yellow to brown

searchTerms: late coming in of adult teeth

occasional.symptomName: Malocclusion due to altered tooth morphology
searchTerms: bite problems from tooth shape changes

occasional.symptomName: Increased risk of dental caries secondary to enamel defects
searchTerms: higher cavity risk from enamel defects
more tooth decay due to weak enamel

rare.notes: Enlarged pulp chambers reported in some families

rare.symptomName: Hypersensitivity leading to chronic dental pain

laboratory: Genetic testing identifying mutations in MMP20, KLK4, or other AI-associated genes
imaging: Dental radiographs showing enamel with radiodensity similar to dentin
genetic: Autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns
other: Clinical examination revealing enamel with mottled opaque discoloration and reduced hardness

distinguishingFeatures: Enamel is thin or absent rather than normal thickness
Surface is smooth or pitted rather than mottled opaque
Enamel is of normal thickness but very soft and poorly mineralized
Enamel easily lost soon after eruption
Radiographs show enamel with very low radiodensity

redFlags: Severe enamel loss leading to rapid tooth wear and functional impairment
Early onset dental sensitivity interfering with feeding or oral hygiene
Family history suggestive of hereditary enamel defects
